text:
frank: quick bakeoff summary for galleon-10b mixed-precision run (mpp-int5). looking for routing + scorecard recs for GTN/product
yasmin: top-line numbers?
frank: p50 46ms, p95 198ms (2k batching); sustained throughput ~720 tok/s; est cost $0.0027 per 1k tokens. int8 baseline p50 41ms p95 160ms throughput 780 tok/s cost $0.0059 per 1k tokens
junaid: wow ~54% cost reduction. any quality regressions?
frank: GTN 2.5k sample sweep: overall instruction-following -0.5% abs, multi-step generation consistency -1.7%, code-refactor hallucinations +1.6% on small snippets
claire: multi-step consistency regression could impact editor flows. are failures prompt-length dependent?
frank: yes — few-shot prompts with >6 examples see divergence. token-level ppl drifts after 800 tokens. deterministic decoding (top-p->0.0 temp->0.2) narrows gap on many slices
metrics-bot: snapshot: candidate galleon-mpp-int5 smoke -> metrics: cost_down, latency_tail_up, error_rate nominal at ts=3602467950
junaid: routing idea: confidence-gated rerun. flow: run mpp-int5 by default; if model_confidence < 0.65 OR confidence_std > 0.12 -> re-run on int8 with lower temp and ensemble decode. keeps cost savings but protects fragile outputs
claire: how compute model_confidence cheaply? we have cheap token-level surprisal aggregator from runtime that runs in <1ms overhead. good starting point
yasmin: alternative: flow-based gating + confidence. map high-assurance endpoints (billing, legal, search-snippets, code-edit) to int8; otherwise mpp-int5 with confidence fallback. also cap context to 1024 for mpp-int5
junaid: agree. also add conditional n-best rerank: generate n=3 on mpp-int5, if top_score_margin < 0.08 then re-rank with int8 LM scoring (cheap)
frank: we'll need a scorecard before GTN review. suggested CSV cols: slice, sample_n, metric (acc/consistency/hallu/latency_p95/cost_per_1k), int8_value, mpp_value, delta_abs, acceptable_threshold, routing_rule, confidence_metric_note
claire: include a short tech note on "few-shot fragility" and recommended mitigations: deterministic decoding, few-shot pruning, and example-level priming templates
yasmin: ops TODO: create flag galleon-mpp-canary, implement confidence metric export, hook rerun path, add dashboards: p95 by variant, rerun-rate, confidence_histogram, hallucination_rate_by_slice
metrics-bot: baseline snapshots saved for galleon-mpp-int5 vs galleon-int8 at ts=3602467955
junaid: canary plan: 60% shadow for 72h to build confidence distribution; start 10% live mpp for non-high-assurance short-context traffic + conditional rerun; monitor 7 days then expand to 40% if stable
frank: product/GTN messaging draft: "New mixed-precision tier: ~50% lower inference cost for general tasks. Fidelity tier (int8) remains default for legal, finance, code and long-context workflows. Routing is transparent to the API with deterministic fallback rules."
yasmin: also include pricing examples and estimated monthly savings for typical mid-tier (~200M tokens/mo) and enterprise (1B tokens/mo) customers
junaid: capture redacted worst-case diffs (esp. code refactor examples) and attach to CSV: https://gist.github.com/redwood/galleon-mpp-examples (redacted)
claire: monitoring thresholds: alert if hallucination_delta > +1.2% OR p95 increase > +15% OR rerun_rate > 2% sustained over 30m. auto-fallback to int8 on any high-severity hallucination signal
frank: I'll assemble CSV + one-pager today and post. please review routing rules and confidence thresholds. :thumbsup:
